before:
New Mexico's main airport, known locally as the Sunport, 3 miles south east of downtown Albuquerque between the Rio Grande and the Sandia Mountains. It handles around 5.5 million passengers and over 400 flights a day.

Southwest is the dominant airline, carrying over half of all passengers, alongside Alaska, American, Delta, JetBlue, United and Advanced Air.

It has more local character than most American airports. Alongside the national chains the concessions are full of New Mexico names: Laguna Burger, Sadie's, Indian Pueblo Kitchen, New Mexico Piñon Coffee and local craft brewers among them. The building itself is a low-lying structure rather than the usual glass box.

The airport is also the centre of the Air Route Traffic Control Center known as ZAB, which manages the airspace over most of Arizona and New Mexico and parts of Colorado, Oklahoma and Texas.

It sits directly west of Kirtland Air Force Base and Sandia National Laboratories.
after:
New Mexico's main airport, known locally as the Sunport, a few miles south east of downtown Albuquerque. It handled about 5.3 million passengers in 2025.

Southwest is the dominant airline, carrying about half of all passengers, alongside Alaska, American, Delta, JetBlue, United and Advanced Air.

It has more local character than most American airports. Alongside the national chains the concessions are full of New Mexico names: Laguna Burger, Sadie's, Indian Pueblo Kitchen, New Mexico Piñon Coffee and local craft brewers among them. The building itself is in a distinct southwestern style rather than the usual glass box.

It sits directly west of Kirtland Air Force Base.

claims.inAfter: It handled about 5.3 million passengers in 2025.
claims.note: Was 'around 5.5 million', which matches the operator's fiscal 2024 total (5,471,678). TOTAL passengers, arrivals plus departures: the operator gives 5,274,764 for calendar 2025 (its monthly table adds up to 5,311,482; both round to 5.3 million). The FAA's preliminary CY2025 table counts 2,562,028 revenue enplanements (boardings only, about half of total passengers, down 4.77 per cent), consistent with it.

claims.inAfter: Southwest is the dominant airline, carrying about half of all passengers
claims.note: Was 'over half'. BTS gives Southwest 50.25 per cent of passengers on US flights in the twelve months to June 2026, with American next on 12.62 per cent. The operator's monthly share was 53.6 per cent in December 2025 and 48.9 per cent in July 2026, so it now hovers around half. The operator's tables list airlines alphabetically with the figures in the same order (Southwest is the seventh row in both).

claims.wasBefore: 3 miles south east of downtown Albuquerque
claims.why: Fails the coordinates check (3.9 miles in a straight line, ratio 0.77); the FAA says 3 nautical miles (3.5 statute miles). Softened to 'a few miles'; the direction is kept.

claims.claim: between the Rio Grande and the Sandia Mountains
claims.wasBefore: between the Rio Grande and the Sandia Mountains
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; no second source places the airport this way, and it describes most of the city rather than the airport.
Out of date: 5.5 million matches fiscal 2024; calendar 2025 was about 5.3 million (operator, FAA).
Misleading. The operator's 427 a day in 2025 counts every take-off and landing including general aviation and military, and Wikipedia gives only 29 per cent of them as scheduled commercial.

claims.wasBefore: carrying over half of all passengers
claims.why: Southwest's share now sits either side of half (48.9 per cent in July 2026, 53.6 per cent in December 2025, 50.25 per cent over the twelve months to June 2026), so 'about half'.

claims.wasBefore: The building itself is a low-lying structure
claims.why: 'Low-lying' rests on Wikipedia alone; the operator's 'distinct southwestern architecture' is kept.

claims.claim: centre of the ZAB air route traffic control center
claims.wasBefore: The airport is also the centre of the Air Route Traffic Control Center known as ZAB, which manages the airspace over most of Arizona and New Mexico and parts of Colorado, Oklahoma and Texas.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and doubtful as worded: the operator's own list of federal facilities at the airport names the control tower and the Flight Standards District Office, not the en-route centre. Of no use to a travel agent either way.
Wikipedia alone; Sandia's own locations page says only that its main site is in Albuquerque. Kirtland's own site refused the request (403).
